subtitle: Journal-club style ICU update: PICO, key results, appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English.

script.heading: Intro
sentences: Welcome to Critical Care Daily for August 02, 2026.
Today we will review 3 recent ICU-relevant publications.
The format is quick listen first, then PICO, key results, critical appraisal, bedside impact, and medical English notes.
Use this as a morning triage tool, then open the source link for full-text appraisal before changing practice.

script.heading: Story 1 - Anabolic androgen therapy in critically ill adults: A systemat
sentences: Story 1 is about Anabolic androgen therapy in critically ill adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis..
This is a systematic review / meta-analysis from Journal of critical care.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in critically ill populations on patient-important outcomes and identify design limitations to inform future studies, how should we interpret ding English language articles enrolling adults (≥18 years) admitted to ICU where anabolic androgen therapies (AAT) were compared with placebo or standard of care. Studies had to report at least one of: mortality, ICU and hospital lengths of stay, or dura?

We searched for randomized control trials (RCTs) through Medline, Embase, and EBM Reviews databases from inception through February 24, 2026, including English language articles enrolling adults (≥18 years) admitted to ICU where anabolic androgen therapies (AAT) were compared with placebo or standard of care.
Studies had to report at least one of: mortality, ICU and hospital lengths of stay, or duration of mechanical ventilation.

Together, we judged risk of bias as 'some concerns' in 3 trials and 'high' in the final trial, and ultimately found that the effects of anabolic-androgen therapy on patient-important outcomes uncertain.
For critical appraisal, focus on whether the design supports a causal conclusion and whether the patients resemble your ICU population.

The bedside implication is this: Potentially practice-relevant because a patient-centered outcome is reported; check absolute risk difference, adverse events, and whether your ICU population matches the study.

script.heading: Story 2 - Balanced crystalloids versus saline and mortality in hospitali
sentences: Story 2 is about Balanced crystalloids versus saline and mortality in hospitalized patients: a hierarchical Bayesian meta-analysis of cluster-randomized trials..
This is a systematic review / meta-analysis from Journal of critical care.

The clinical question is best framed as follows: in Critically ill or ICU-relevant patients described in the abstract; confirm eligibility criteria in the full text., how should we interpret Balanced crystalloids compared with saline and mortality in hospitalized patients: a hierarchical Bayesian meta-analysis of cluster-randomized trials?
Six trials involving 42,223 patients met the inclusion criteria.
For mortality, the pooled Bayesian relative effect was 0.92 (95% CrI 0.77-1.18), corresponding to an 83% posterior probability of benefit.
For AKI, the pooled Bayesian relative effect was 1.02 (95% CrI 0.86-1.23), corresponding to a 40% posterior probability of benefit.

The bedside implication is this: This is relevant to default ICU fluid choice; focus on absolute mortality difference, kidney outcomes, and whether the enrolled population matches your resuscitation patients.

script.heading: Outro

Before applying any finding, check the full source, the absolute effect size, and your local ICU context.

articles.title: Balanced crystalloids versus saline and mortality in hospitalized patients: a hierarchical Bayesian meta-analysis of cluster-randomized trials.
articles.summary: Balanced crystalloids are widely used as alternatives to 0.9% saline, yet their effects on patient-important outcomes remain uncertain. Six trials involving 42,223 patients met the inclusion criteria. For mortality, the pooled Bayesian relative effect was 0.92 (95% CrI 0.77-1.18), corresponding to an 83% posterior probability of benefit. For AKI, the pooled Bayesian relative effect was 1.02 (95% CrI 0.86-1.23), corresponding to a 40% posterior probability of benefit. Balanced crystalloid policies were not associated with a clear reduction in mortality or AKI in cluster-randomized evaluations of routine care.

articles.title: Volume-controlled mechanical ventilation during cardiopulmonary resuscitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.summary: To assess the evidence on volume-controlled mechanical ventilation versus manual ventilation or other ventilation modes during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). Randomized trials and non-randomized studies in children or adults with cardiac arrest and an advanced airway were included. We screened 12,004 abstracts and included 13 articles consisting of six trials enrolling 461 patients and seven non-randomized studies including 4607 patients. Meta-analysis of 120 patients from two randomized trials comparing volume-controlled to manual ventilation showed no difference for return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) (odds ratio, 1.31; 95%-confidence interval, 0.64-2.71). Non-randomized studies were at serious or critical risk of bias.
